title: Trigun: Balance of the Universe — Interactive Graphic Mystery Kit
format: Story-led mythological detective puzzle kit (NOT a magazine): graphic novel + mystery envelopes + clue-solving game + Indian-mythology learning kit + hands-on activity box.
generated_from: trigun kibookal storyline.pdf (story / source of truth)
trigun kibookal page list .pdf (materials + envelope structure)

components.style_swappable: ANY KBS style may be used; the LAYOUT stays identical because layout lives in the templates, not the style.

design_principles: Every output is a FLAT printable A5 image (or a 4cm square puzzle piece) — no physical-object framing.
LAYOUT is locked and style-independent: the same template renders the same composition in any visual style.
VISUAL STYLE is swappable: KBS040 is the native look; the user may try the same kit in any other KBS style.
CHARACTER CONSISTENCY is mandatory: every character render copies its locked appearance + reference card.
Premium, mysterious, tactile, Indian, kid-friendly throughout.

compose_order: 3. page content_slots filled in (titles, text, percentages, code words, hidden messages)
4. for each character on the page: inject character.lock_line + attach character.ref_images
5. chosen style DNA (medium/linework/palette/texture/finish) from the style_lock
render_protocol.reference_attachment_rule: When rendering in the NATIVE style (KBS040), also attach the template-s layout_reference image for maximum composition fidelity. When rendering in a DIFFERENT style, do NOT attach the native layout_reference (it would drag the native look); rely on the structure_block + that style-s own refs + character refs so the LAYOUT repeats while the LOOK changes.
render_protocol.aspect: A5 pages render at 3:4; puzzle pieces render at 1:1.
render_protocol.consistency: Always attach character ref cards for any page featuring a character; keep face/hair/costume/colour identical across pages.

world_glossary.Ekta: 13-year-old protagonist, the Dhar Rakshak (book-protector); decodes the clues.
world_glossary.Bramhaanda Vichaar: The ancient book that holds the original record of how the universe works; carries the map and the riddle.
world_glossary.the three gunas: Rajas (initiating), Tamas (sustaining/dissolving), Sattva (clarity) — the three forces of all material existence.
world_glossary.the Asuras: Disguised as sages, they tricked the three forces and stole the Codes ~400 years ago, hiding each fragment in the place most OPPOSITE to its guna.
world_glossary.Mara / Mahamoha: The antagonist — the Other Voice / Dharakshak; mocks and tempts.
world_glossary.Dadi: Ekta-s grandmother; kept the haveli and the book.
world_glossary.the Codes: Frequency/word patterns defining each guna; the puzzle pieces the player collects.
world_glossary.Pancha Mahabhutas: The five elements — the picture formed when all 22 code pieces are arranged correctly.

physical_kit.main_graphic_novel: 1 (cover -> intro poem -> story -> character cards -> map card)
physical_kit.puzzle_pieces: 22 squares of 4cm x 4cm (7 red Rajas + 7 green Sattva + 7 blue Tamas + 1 yellow final) -> assemble to Pancha Mahabhutas

MAIN_BOOK.name: Front cover
MAIN_BOOK.content: FRONT COVER. Title TRIGUN large; subtitle Balance of the Universe; Ekta center holding the ancient book before a faded Rajasthani haveli; three faint guna spirits behind her (fiery-red Jwalika, black Mohika, white Suchi); a small Ages 11-13 badge in a lower corner; tagline An Interactive Graphic Mystery Kit along the bottom.

MAIN_BOOK.name: Intro poem sheet
MAIN_BOOK.content: ART ONLY: a decorated aged-parchment poem sheet — engraved-serif heading area at top, a small three-guna ornament, a fine red/ochre border, and a CLEAR empty central panel for the poem (do NOT draw poem text; the full poem is added later as editable text). Order locked Rajas -> Tamas -> Sattva (see production lock).

MAIN_BOOK.name: Story 1 — The Arrival
MAIN_BOOK.content: A 4-panel comic page. P1: Ekta in a car, chin on hand, watching Rajasthani dust blur past, sulking — caption: The summer Ekta turned thirteen, the promise of Manali became a haveli in Rajasthan. P2: an old haveli gate; caretaker Bhola Kaka opens it and pulls her parents into talk about the water tank. P3: Ekta quietly slips into the stone courtyard. P4: she wanders deep, confusing corridors — caption: Old havelis are built for wandering. Speech: father — You will like it.

MAIN_BOOK.name: Story 2 — The Book
MAIN_BOOK.content: A 4-panel comic page. P1: a narrow easy-to-miss door at the end of a dim corridor, caption A narrow, easy-to-miss door... P2: a small windowless room, a bundle wrapped in cloud-grey cloth on the floor. P3: the cloth has fallen away to reveal an ancient cracked dark-leather book carved with strange symbols. P4: Ekta kneels and opens the book — dense maps, force diagrams, partial Sanskrit and modern Hindi margin notes — speech This... this is everything!, caption The word book was insufficient.

MAIN_BOOK.name: Story 3 — The Three
MAIN_BOOK.content: A 4-panel comic page. P1: Ekta looks up startled, speech off-panel You could have been gentler with the cover. P2: three hazy semi-translucent figures against three walls — Jwalika in rippling red-gold with a clay pot, Mohika tall in black with a glass bottle, Suchi in plain white sitting still. P3: close on Suchi (warm natural skin, white sari) opening her eyes, speech Ekta. We have been waiting for you. P4: Ekta sits on the dusty floor, speech Alright. Start from the beginning., caption The book knows you. It always has.

MAIN_BOOK.name: Story 4 — The Theft
MAIN_BOOK.content: A 4-panel comic page. P1: a small triad diagram — the three were the grammar of the universe: Rajas initiating, Tamas sustaining and dissolving, Sattva giving clarity. P2: the Asuras arrive disguised as soft-spoken sages in ochre robes, bowing like scholars. P3: they ask careful questions; each honest answer turns a hidden lock, shown as a key turning slowly. P4: the three realise too late — caption: By the time we understood, the Codes had been separated from us. The preparation took centuries; the taking was very fast.

MAIN_BOOK.name: Story 5 — The Crack
MAIN_BOOK.content: A 4-panel comic page. P1: an Asura sings a mocking song while leaving, a scrap of rhyme floating. P2: Ekta thinking hard, speech They were proud. Proud people hide things in plain sight. P3: an insight sketch — each fragment hidden in the place most OPPOSITE its guna (fire hidden where things rot). P4: Ekta kneels over the hand-drawn map from the book, the haveli at its centre with concentric rings, Suchi (white) beside her, speech So. Where do we start?

MAIN_BOOK.name: Jaisalmer map (loose card)
MAIN_BOOK.content: JAISALMER QUEST MAP & BOARD. Dadi-s Haveli at the centre with concentric rings. EXACTLY eight distinct named markers around it, each labelled once: Bhangarh Fort, Library, Garden, Archaeological Society of India, Main Market, Landfill, Desert, Dadi-s Haveli. Compass rose, titled JAISALMER cartouche, faint paths. No duplicate labels.
